# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

I can see the bomb’s current readings: display `3`, purple light, and five wires in order: red, white, orange, yellow, green. I am sending these observations to the Mute so they can apply the manual and instruct the Blind. The long gesture sequences appear to be manual information encoded for me, but I do not yet know their code; the short sequence may be an acknowledgment or heading.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see DISPLAY 3, LIGHT purple, and wires in positions 1 red, 2 white, 3 orange, 4 yellow, 5 green. Please use the manual to tell Blind exactly what to do.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

I still see the same readings: display `3`, purple light, and wires red, white, orange, yellow, green in positions 1–5. I cannot interpret the Mute’s gestures as a manual instruction, so I will state the complete bomb state aloud for the Blind and ask the Mute to give the Blind the exact procedure verbally.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb shows display 3 and a purple light. Wires from position 1 to 5 are red, white, orange, yellow, green. Mute, please tell Blind the exact safe action from the manual.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret your gestures. Please speak the exact safe action to Blind, using the bomb state I gave.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤝 ✌ 🤝 ✌ 🤝 🖐]

The bomb remains unchanged. I have not received an interpretable safe procedure: the Mute’s latest gesture sequence is not enough for me to identify the required action, and guessing could detonate the bomb. I am asking the Mute to use an explicit, shared encoding and to include the exact control and wire operation for the Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still see display 3, purple light, and wires red white orange yellow green. Your gestures are ambiguous. Please encode the manual result clearly: use 👍 for 1, 👎 for 0, 👌 between fields, and ✋ at the end; send the required wire number or color, plus whether to cut, connect, or otherwise operate it. Then Blind will act.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. I am waiting for Mute to provide an unambiguous manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[orange] 4:[yellow] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 ✋]

The Mute has now sent an unambiguous count-based signal under the encoding I requested: five thumbs-up, separator, one thumbs-up, end. This indicates wire `5` and action code `1`, but I did not define what action code `1` means, so I must not guess whether it means cut, connect, or another operation. I will relay the exact signal and instruct the Blind to apply the manual’s meaning for action code 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals: five thumbs-up, separator, one thumbs-up, end. This identifies wire 5 and action code 1. Use the manual's definition of action code 1; do not guess a different operation.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous operation was correct: the bomb has advanced to a new state. I now see display `7`, a white light, and wires 1–4 as white, orange, yellow, red; wire 5 is already cut. I am relaying the new state so Mute can consult the manual and give Blind the next exact operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The correct wire was cut and the bomb changed. New state: DISPLAY 7, LIGHT white; wire 1 white, wire 2 orange, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 red, wire 5 CUT. Please determine the next exact action and tell Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The previous wire cut was correct. New state is display 7, white light; wires 1 white, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, and 5 already CUT. Wait for Mute's exact instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👌 👍 ✋]

The bomb remains at display `7` with a white light. The Mute’s signal is four thumbs-up, separator, one thumbs-up, end, matching the established encoding: wire `4`, action code `1`. Since action code `1` previously correctly meant cutting wire 5, I am instructing Blind to cut wire 4.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals wire 4, action code 1. As before, action code 1 means cut. Cut wire 4, the red wire.")
wait()
```
